method: HUMAN runs the KiCad pcb_calculator GUI (Track Width tab), IPC-2221 versions only (7.0 to 10.0 branch per docs/research/kicad-pcb-calculator.md section 5; NOT master, whose app uses the Brooks and Adam IPC-2152 fit, a different model than our legacy Mode B). Record Help > About version string and OS in toolVersion. Copper thickness is typed in mm in the tool and given as thickness_um to our adapter, so no oz-to-thickness convention can cause a mismatch. Widths are read in mm, as displayed (all displayed digits). Inputs and outputs per docs/validation/crosscheck-phase1.md section 2. Do not type numbers from memory or from our app. A pass verifies no ledger row.

toolInputsAsTyped.flow: type the current and the temperature rise; read the width in the External column (width in mm)

compare.why: Derived before any run, not tuned: same constants as ledger S-001 (k 0.048/0.024, exponents 0.44/0.725) and thickness typed in mm so no oz convention applies (docs/research/kicad-pcb-calculator.md section 2, values consistent with 1 mil = 0.0254 mm); the only expected difference is rounding of the displayed digits. 1e-5 = half a unit of the 6th decimal in mm (as in the K-IMG7 screenshot) divided by the smallest width in this file (about 0.05 mm, a lower bound, not a result). If the tool shows fewer than 6 decimals, or this is KiCad master (Brooks and Adam fit, a different model), the human must recompute or reclassify BEFORE running (worksheet section 2.4).

compare.why: Derived before any run, not tuned: same constants and thickness as the width cases (no oz convention, no resistivity involved); only rounding of the displayed current. 1e-4 assumes at least 5 significant digits displayed (worst-case half-unit 5e-5). If fewer are displayed, the human recomputes 0.5 x 10^-(s-1) BEFORE the first run and edits this value (worksheet section 2.4).
